introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i)(a) The rate of increase of the surface area of a sphere is $36\pi\ \text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$ at the instant when the radius is $3$ cm. Find the rate of increase of the radius of the sphere. *[3 marks]*

[The surface area of a sphere, $A=4\pi r^2$ and the volume of a sphere, $V=\frac43\pi r^3$.]
questions.corrige_markdown:
$A=4\pi r^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dr}=8\pi r.$

Chain rule: $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{dA}{dr}\times\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

At $r=3$: $36\pi=8\pi(3)\times\dfrac{dr}{dt}=24\pi\,\dfrac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{36}{24}=1.5.$

**The radius increases at $1.5\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i)(b) With the same sphere (surface area increasing at $36\pi\ \text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$ when the radius is $3$ cm), find the rate of increase of the volume of the sphere. *[3 marks]*

[The surface area of a sphere, $A=4\pi r^2$ and the volume of a sphere, $V=\frac43\pi r^3$.]
(ii) The area enclosed by the curve $y=\sqrt{x+3}$ and the $x$-axis, from $x=1$ to $x=2$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of the solid generated. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Volume of revolution about the $x$-axis: $V=\pi\displaystyle\int_a^b y^2\,dx$.

Here $y^2=x+3$, so

$V=\pi\displaystyle\int_1^2(x+3)\,dx=\pi\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}+3x\right]_1^2.$

At $x=2$: $\dfrac{4}{2}+6=8$. At $x=1$: $\dfrac12+3=3.5$.

$V=\pi(8-3.5)=4.5\pi.$

**The volume is $\dfrac{9\pi}{2}\approx14.1$ cubic units.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) Three particles of masses 3 kg, 2 kg and 1 kg are at the points with coordinates $(-1,3)$, $(5,2)$ and $(-1,-4)$ respectively. Find the coordinates of the centre of gravity of these three particles. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total mass $=3+2+1=6$ kg.

$\bar x=\dfrac{\sum mx}{\sum m}=\dfrac{3(-1)+2(5)+1(-1)}{6}=\dfrac{-3+10-1}{6}=\dfrac66=1.$

$\bar y=\dfrac{\sum my}{\sum m}=\dfrac{3(3)+2(2)+1(-4)}{6}=\dfrac{9+4-4}{6}=\dfrac96=1.5.$

**The centre of gravity is at $(1,\ 1.5)$.**
